name: Green Beans (Bush)
description: A warm-season crop that produces an abundant harvest of tender pods over a few weeks. Bush varieties are compact and do not require a trellis.
tips: After the soil has warmed, plant seeds directly in the garden. Avoid disturbing the roots. Water at the base to prevent leaf diseases.
succession: Sow new seeds every 2-3 weeks until mid-summer for a continuous harvest throughout the season.
yield: Continuous harvest over several weeks. A 10-foot row can produce 3-5 lbs of beans.

soil.notes: Legumes fix their own nitrogen from the air. Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers, which will result in excessive foliage and fewer beans.

temperature.notes: A warm-season crop. Do not plant until soil has warmed and all danger of frost has passed. Flowers may drop in extreme heat.

environmentalAlerts.message: Cover with a blanket or bring potted plants indoors to protect from frost.

storage.notes: Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer. For long-term storage, beans can be blanched and frozen, canned, or pickled.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Monitor for Mexican bean beetles
careTasks.description: Check the undersides of leaves for yellow egg clusters and lacy, damaged foliage. Hand-pick adults and eggs.

careTasks.name: Harvest beans regularly
careTasks.description: Pick beans when they are firm, crisp, and about the thickness of a pencil. Harvest every few days to encourage the plant to produce more.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Beans need consistent moisture, especially when flowering and forming pods. Water when the top inch of soil is dry. Avoid overhead watering to prevent disease.

name: Peas
wateringNeeds: Consistent moisture, especially during flowering and pod set
description: A classic cool-season crop and one of the first to be planted in spring. Varieties include shelling peas, edible-podded snow peas, and crisp snap peas.
tips: Harvest pods when they are plump and sweet for best flavor. Pods left on the vine too long become starchy and tough.
succession: Make 2-3 sowings 10-14 days apart in early spring for a longer harvest. Can also be planted in late summer for a fall crop.
yield: Harvest over 2-3 weeks. A 10-foot row can produce 2-4 lbs of shelled peas.

soil.notes: As legumes, peas fix their own nitrogen. Inoculating seeds with rhizobia bacteria at planting time can boost growth, especially in new gardens.

temperature.notes: A cool-season crop. Plant as soon as the soil can be worked in spring. Dislikes summer heat, which stops pod production.

environmentalAlerts.message: Peas can tolerate a light frost, but cover if a hard freeze is expected to protect blossoms and young pods.

storage.notes: The sugars in peas quickly turn to starch after picking, so eat or preserve them as soon as possible. Store in a perforated plastic bag.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Inoculate seeds (optional)
careTasks.description: Before planting, coat seeds with a rhizobial inoculant powder to help the plants fix nitrogen more effectively.

careTasks.name: Install trellis at planting
careTasks.description: For vining varieties, set up a trellis or other support at planting time to give the vines a structure to climb on as they grow.

careTasks.name: Harvest pods regularly
careTasks.description: Harvest snow peas when pods are flat, snap peas when plump, and shelling peas when pods are rounded and full. Frequent picking encourages more production.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Peas need cool, moist soil to thrive. Water consistently, especially as they begin to flower and form pods, to ensure a sweet, plump harvest. Water when the top inch of soil feels dry.
